To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the workload characteristics of Google traces are not representative of Hadoop applications, (2) the impact of the job scheduling policies on the performance of Hadoop applications is not as significant as previously thought, and (3) the performance of HDFS can be significantly improved by using local disk storage instead of the shared storage.

(1) the traces from Google can be used to generate realistic workloads for Hadoop, (2) the Hadoop scheduler that performs the best is the default FIFO scheduler, and (3) the impact of shared network storage on Hadoop performance depends on the workload.

the traces from Google can be used to infer the following key insights: (i) The distribution of the job sizes in a Hadoop cluster can be modeled as a log-normal distribution, and (ii), the distribution of the job inter-arrival times can be modeled as an exponential distribution.
